blocks.text: Good to know about Fairfield Island

items.t: There are no SnapStats numbers for Fairfield Island — anyone quoting one is quoting nothing.

"Island" is a local name with no published boundary in the sources checked. The City plans the area (Schedule B2, with Chilliwack Proper), but its exact boundaries and dike geography are not confirmed on an official source — treat any precise boundary line in listing copy as unconfirmed.

A detached house here can still come with a strata fee. The Williams Road example sits in a 6-unit bare-land strata described in its listing as carrying a minimal fee — a buyer who assumes "detached = no strata" misses the corporation, its bylaws and its Form B entirely.

The flood question is open. Unlike areas where a floodplain bylaw position can be cited, Fairfield Island's dike and flood-construction-level facts are not confirmed (City sources could not be reached). A seller's reassurance is not a substitute for the City's own parcel check.

The plan pairing surprises people: Fairfield Island is not planned on its own — its neighbourhood plan is the joint Schedule B2 "Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan," so plan searches run under only "Fairfield Island" miss documents filed under Chilliwack Proper.

Provincial dates that changed a bare-land strata lot's rule book here: rental bylaws void November 24, 2022; wider 55+ exemptions May 1, 2023; 10% CRF minimum November 1, 2023; depreciation reports every five years from July 1, 2024; Chilliwack SSMUH Bylaw 5395 adopted June 18, 2024.

Chilliwack property taxes (city ground only): notices are mailed at the end of May and taxes are due the first working day after July 1; a 5% penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026. items.t: The "island" is a slough, not the Fraser River, that makes it an island in daily life. The Schedule B-2 plan states Fairfield Island is separated from the rest of Chilliwack Proper by the Hope Slough, is currently accessible only via road bridges at Menzies and Young Roads, and will add a planned pedestrian and cyclist bridge at Williams Street — every trip to the hospital and the downtown stock crosses one of those two bridges.

The plan expects infill, not a townhouse project. The Schedule B-2 framework addresses infill development opportunities — redevelopment of existing large lots into smaller-lot single detached, duplex or row housing, some convenience commercial, and new attached housing along Hope River Road — and notes there are limited commercial services within the neighbourhood at present. No townhouse complex for Fairfield Island appears in any source checked.

Fairfield Island's housing era is stated in the City's own plan. The Schedule B-2 plan characterises the current building stock as predominantly one- and two-storey 1970s–1980s detached homes — a buyer here is buying a house of that era, with a house inspection to match, not a strata purchase with a depreciation report.

items.t: SSMUH / suites / accessory dwellings (Chilliwack specifics): the SSMUH amendment is ESTABLISHED — Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395 amended Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 and was adopted June 18, 2024, as recorded in s. 14's amendment record in the consolidated Zoning Bylaw 5000 ( item 6). Suite/ADU figures confirmed in the same verification (item 7f, citing Zoning Bylaw 5000, ss. 2, 4.06, 5.04): a secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the principal dwelling, one accessory dwelling unit is permitted per lot, garden suites are capped at 100 m², and parking rules sit at s. 5.04. Application to any specific parcel remains a per-parcel check.

ALR block — full form (the northern/eastern perimeter where ALR ground exists): properties in the Agricultural Land Reserve are subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act and ALR regulations; ALC approval may be required before the City can approve related development applications, and the City directs owners to check ALR status on the City Webmap; an ALC application may be required for a new house, coach house or suite, for placing fill or removing soil, for non-farm uses, and for subdivision or a boundary adjustment, with ALC applications referred to the City for review. Subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: principal residence ≤500 m² total floor area; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm Home Plate: OCP Development Permit Area 4 exists to reduce the long-term impact of residential uses on agricultural land, and a Development Permit is required when the Zoning Bylaw's Farm Home Plate regulations are not met. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" line is an error and is not used here.

: Form B (SPA s. 123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw. Pure freehold detached purchases have no Form B; diligence runs on title, permits and the flood/ALR checks instead.

Speculation and vacancy taxes: no speculation- or vacancy-tax position for a Fairfield Island parcel is documented in this area's research — none is imported. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax at 3% is vancouver only and does not apply here.

items.t: The plan name does quiet work: Fairfield Island does not have its own neighbourhood plan — it is planned jointly with Chilliwack Proper under Schedule B2, so the document a buyer should read for this ground covers the older city core as well, and "Fairfield Island policy" usually means a B2 passage written for both areas at once.
